To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fitness landscape of a graph bipartition problem is very complex and that the structure of a dependency graph, describing the gene interactions, is a good indicator for the difficulty of an evolutionary algorithm.
the search space of the graph biparitioning problem is very rugged and contains many local minima.
The search space of graph bipartition is very different depending on the graph structure and the representation of a graph in an EA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the structure of the fitness landscape of a problem, and how this structure influences the performance of an evolutionary algorithm.
a detailed analysis of the structure of fitness landscapes and the design of efficient search heuristics based on this analysis.
understanding the structure of the problem, and how the structure influences the performance of different types of algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no one best algorithm, but rather that the choice of the algorithm depends on the characteristics of the problem instance.
the fitness landscape of the problem is not only influenced by the epistasis of the problem, but that the structure of a graph is a much more important characteristic.
there is no single best algorithm for all types of graph bipartitionings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a greedy operator is very effective for structured graphs, but for unstructured graphs, the memetic algorithm is the only effective approach.
the structure of a problem is more important than its size.
the fitness landscape of the problem is highly structured and that the performance of an evolutionary algorithm is significantly influenced by the characteristics of the dependency graph.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of evolutionary algorithms is not only dependent on the fitness landscape, but on the structure of the representation as well.

the performance of a heuristic algorithm for a combinatorial optimization problem can be predicted from the fitness landscape of the problem, and that this prediction can be obtained without solving the problem.

, in order to design an effective algorithm for the problem of graph bipartition, one must understand the underlying fitness landscape of the problem, and that a simple local search algorithm may not always be the right choice.
